candidates.locator: Page 19, Section part_i, sludge monitoring frequency table
candidates.exact_span:
1,500 ≤ Sludge < 15,000                        Once/Two Months
   15,000 ≤ Sludge                                Once/Month
   *Amount of sewage sludge placed on an active sewage sludge unit (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The sludge-amount thresholds and frequencies determine which monitoring schedule applies; different readings of the dry-weight sludge quantity band or the meaning of 'Once/Two Months' would change which monitoring obligations are deemed required for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span:
Representative samples of sewage sludge shall be collected and analyzed in accordance with the
   methods referenced in 40 CFR 503.8(b).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a sampling and analysis obligation and the evidentiary standard for results; interpreting whether representative sampling occurred, or whether 503.8(b) methods were used, changes whether monitoring was required and whether absent results are documented no-data, inadequate evidence, or unresolved.

candidates.locator: Page 19, Section part_i, Section II paragraph 1
candidates.exact_span:
1. Pollutant limits - Sewage sludge shall not be applied to a surface disposal site if the
      concentrations of the listed pollutants exceed the corresponding values based on the surface
      disposal site boundary to the property line distance:
candidates.computation_change_reason: This operative limit ties enforceable numeric pollutant caps to site-boundary-to-property-line distance; different interpretations of 'applied,' 'surface disposal site,' or how distance is measured would change which Table 5 limit applies and whether a reported concentration is compared for compliance.

candidates.exact_span:
Table 5
       Unit boundary to property line                 Pollutant concentrations* (mg/kg)
       distance (meter)                     Arsenic        Chromium        Nickel       PCB’s
       0 to < 25                              30              200           210          49
       25 to < 50                             34              220           240          49
       50 to < 75                             39              260           270          49
       75 to < 100                            46              300           320          49
       100 to < 125                           53              360           390          49
       125 to < 150                           62              450           420          49
       ≥ 150                                  73              600           420          49
candidates.computation_change_reason: Each distance band assigns distinct numeric limits for arsenic, chromium, nickel, and PCBs; assigning a site to a different band or parameter column changes the applicable enforceable limit used to evaluate reported measurements.
Whether pollutant concentrations and comparisons are on a dry-weight basis affects how reported sludge analytical results are normalized before comparison to Table 5 limits.

candidates.locator: Page 19, Section part_i, Section II paragraph 2
candidates.exact_span: 2. Management practices - Listed in Section I.B. above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cross-reference incorporates external management-practice requirements that may include additional monitoring or conditional obligations; resolving what Section I.B. requires changes which monitoring duties are treated as applicable.

candidates.locator: Page 19, Section part_i, Section II paragraph 4.a
candidates.exact_span:
a. The distance of the surface disposal site from the property line and the concentration
          (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed above in Table 5, as well as the applicable
          pollutant concentration criteria listed in Table 5.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Recorded site distance and pollutant concentrations determine which Table 5 limit is selected for compliance comparison, and the presence or absence of these retained records affects whether missing numeric results can be classified as documented no-data versus required monitoring lacking adequate evidence.

candidates.locator: Page 19, Section part_i, Section II paragraph 4.b
candidates.exact_span:
b. A certification statement that all applicable requirements (specifically listed) have been met,
          and that the permittee understands that there are significant penalties for false certification
          including fine and imprisonment. See 503.27(a)(1)(ii) or 503.27(a)(2)(ii) as applicable to the
          permittees sludge disposal activities.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a filed certification exists, which 503.27 subsection applies, and whether it is treated as documentary evidence versus a substitute for numeric results affects how periods without ordinary reported measurements are classified under missing-evidence semantics.
